notes: Building and Engineering News, vol. 19 part 2 (Internet Archive buildingengine1921919cont, an item id that breaks the pattern), the 27 weekly issues from 2 July to 31 December 1919. Same method as the later volumes: every numbered entry under Building Permit Applications and Building Contracts was taken from the djvu.xml OCR, East Bay headings set aside, and each San Francisco lot built from the block corner on the DPW street centrelines and compared with the sf-parcels shapes; a placement was accepted where the lot starts within two feet of a lot line of today (or the record names an unambiguous corner) and the roll dates the building 1918-1921, and alterations were matched by printed street number in sf-eas-addresses where the roll dates the building before 1919. Every published row was read against the page image, location first; most of the 195 rows read needed a name, a cost or the wording corrected, and a cost or name that could not be read on the image was left out. Entries cut by a column break were read on in the next column. Descriptions of rows marked confidence low were built from the OCR and have not been read against the image. Owners are private individuals and are cut everywhere (raw.note; scrub_owner.py removes the fragments the OCR garbles past the first cut); a firm or institution named as owner is kept, and where the contractor, architect or engineer named is the owner, shares the owner's surname or is listed at the owner's premises that name is cut too. Sub-trade contracts are timeline entries and set no builder credit. Completion notices, liens, sub-contracts printed 'on above' and the news columns were not taken. The paper came out on Wednesdays and the pages carry no dated running head, so issue dates are set from the cover dates (issues.json beside the corpus: first leaf of each issue; four covers the OCR missed are interpolated a week apart). Permits whose heading counts more than one dwelling (7) were set aside before the image check and sit with the held single houses, as do two single houses that were read against the image and have no name left to publish. Three held rows of later volumes (October 1924, August 1929, April 1931) whose parcels got a page from this volume were read against the image and published in their own files.

coverage.remaining: Vols. 19 pt. 2 to 31 read (July 1919 to January 1932); the 9 half-year volumes before July 1919 (1915 to June 1919) are unread, buildingengineer1919cont (January to June 1919) next. In this volume: 154 rows placed on a parcel whose roll year fits, single houses with no architect named and no page (7 of them permits for a row of houses), are logged and held until another fact gives the parcel a page (extra.placed_apn; all but two still need the image check). 455 rows have a nearest parcel that was not accepted (the lot starts off today's lot lines, or the roll dates the building outside the window). 673 rows were not placed: location lines not parsed (tract lots, garbled headings), street pairs that do not cross under the names read, and printed street numbers with no EAS row today.
coverage.note: 2,706 numbered entries read, 1,475 San Francisco rows, 802 placed on a parcel, 195 picked and read against the page image, 119 published on 112 pages (48 seeded), 74 held back: 32 alterations with nothing to confirm the street number, 22 storeys, unit counts or uses that contradict the roll, eight pieces of minor work, seven trade contracts for a building already carried by its permit and five repeat listings; two more joined the held houses.
